title: Iminodiacetic acid stabilized 3d-4f clusters: Synthesis, structure, and magnetism
claim: In situ transient [M(IDA)] species (M = Ni or Co), not preformed stable complexes, chelate the 3d ion and then use pendant carboxylate oxygens to direct lanthanide hydrolysis and link further [M(IDA)] units.
explanation: IDA and derivatives provide two carboxylate oxygens and one nitrogen that can complete an octahedral pocket around Ni(II) or Co(II). The resulting [M(IDA)] units protect Ln hydrolysis and can connect through vacant sites on the chelated metal, giving many d-f architectures.
scope: Iminodiacetic acid and derivative ligands with Ni(II) or Co(II) and lanthanides.
conditions: [M(IDA)] forms in situ during synthesis rather than being isolated as a stable precursor.
caveats: The review treats [M(IDA)] as a transient intermediate inferred from assembly behavior, not as an isolated reagent.
